en: The Questions of Milinda: The Section on the Refutation of Difficulties,
from the Chapter of Puzzles.
3. The Question on the Illustration of the Covering of the Private Parts “Venerable Nāgasena, this was said by the Tathāgata:
‘Restraint of the body is good;’”
"Restraint in speech is good;
restraint in mind is good;
restraint in all things is good."
Furthermore, the Tathāgata, having sat in the midst of the fourfold assembly before gods and men, displayed to the brahmin Sela his private parts,
which were enclosed in a sheath. "Venerable Nāgasena, if it was said by the Blessed One,
'Restraint of the body is good,' then that statement that he displayed to the brahmin Sela his private parts, which were enclosed in a sheath, must be false."
“If the Blessed One showed the brahmin Sela his private parts enclosed in a sheath, then the statement ‘Restraint of the body is good’ must be false.
This too is a dilemma from both sides that has come to you; it must be resolved by you.
“Great King, this was indeed spoken by the Blessed One: ‘Restraint of the body is good. And yet the private parts enclosed in a sheath were shown to the brahmin Sela.”
“Great King, for one in whom doubt regarding the Tathāgata has arisen, the Blessed One displays a body corresponding to that [doubt] through his psychic power; only that person sees that miracle.
“But, venerable Nāgasena, who will believe this—that while the entire assembly is present, only one person sees that secret, and the rest, though staying right there, do not see it?
Pray, show me the reason for this; convince me with a logical argument.”
“But have you ever seen, Great King, any sick man surrounded by his relatives and friends?
“Yes, venerable sir.
“Now, Great King, did that assembly see that feeling with which that man was feeling?”
“Certainly not, venerable sir; that man experiences it by himself alone, venerable sir.

“In the same way, great king, for whomsoever doubt has arisen regarding the Tathāgata, the Tathāgata displays a body corresponding to that [doubt] through psychic power for the sake of awakening him; only that person sees that miracle.
Or again, great king, suppose a spirit were to possess some man—would the assembly, great king, see that arrival of the spirit?”
“Certainly not, venerable sir; that very sick man does not see the arrival of that spirit.

“In the same way, great king, for whomsoever doubt has arisen regarding the Tathāgata, it is for his sake that the Tathāgata manifests a body resembling him through psychic power for the purpose of awakening him; only he sees that miracle.
“It was difficult, venerable Nāgasena, what was done by the Blessed One, in that he showed even that which was invisible to one person.”
“Great king, the Blessed One did not show the secret; rather, he showed the shadow of his supernormal power.
“Venerable sir, even when the shadow is seen, the secret is indeed seen, for one has reached a conclusion upon seeing it.
“Moreover, great king, it is difficult for the Tathāgata to awaken those beings who are capable of being awakened.”
If, Great King, the Tathāgata were to neglect his activity, those beings who are capable of being awakened would not awaken.

But because, Great King, the Tathāgata is skilled in application and seeks to awaken those beings capable of being awakened, the Tathāgata awakens those capable of being awakened by whatever means of application through which they may be awakened.
Just as, Great King, a physician and surgeon administers whatever medicine by which a patient becomes healthy—so too does the Tathāgata.
Just as one approaches a patient with that medicine, making them vomit what must be vomited, purging what must be purged,
applying an ointment where it must be applied,
and administering an enema where it must be administered; even so, Great King, the Tathāgata awakens those beings who are to be awakened by whatever means they are awakened through.
Or again, great king, just as a woman with a difficult labor shows her hidden, private parts to a physician;
even so, great king, did the Tathāgata, in order to awaken beings who were capable of being awakened, show through his supernormal power that which is invisible, a shadow-like form.
Great king, there is no such thing as a place that is invisible when taken in relation to a person.

If, Great King, anyone were to awaken upon seeing the heart of the Blessed One, the Blessed One would show his heart through the application of skillful means (*yoga*), for the Tathāgata, Great King, is a knower of skillful means and is skilled in teaching.

Did not the Tathāgata, Great King, knowing the disposition of the elder Nanda, lead him to the abode of the gods and show him the celestial maidens, thinking, "By this means this clansman will awaken," and was it not by that means that the clansman awakened?
"In this way, Great King, the Tathāgata, disparaging, censuring, and loathing the sign of beauty in many ways, displayed the Kakuṭapādī nymphs for the sake of his awakening.
Thus, too, the Tathāgata is skilled in yoga and proficient in teaching.
Furthermore, Great King, when the Elder Cūḷapanthaka had been driven out by his brother..."
Approaching one who was suffering and dejected, he gave him a fine piece of cloth, thinking, "By means of this, this clansman will attain awakening.
And that clansman, by reason of that, attained mastery in the teaching of the Conqueror.
In this way too, Great King, the Tathāgata is skilled in application and expert in teaching.
Furthermore, Great King, when the Tathāgata was asked a question for a third time by the brahmin Mogharāja, he did not answer, thinking:
"In this way, this son of good family’s conceit will be stilled; through the stilling of conceit, there will be realization.
And by that means, the son of good family’s conceit was stilled; through the stilling of conceit, that brahmin attained mastery over the six direct knowledges.
“Even so, Great King, the Tathāgata is skilled in application and expert in teaching.
“Excellent, Bhante Nāgasena! This question has been well-unraveled through manifold reasons;
the thicket has been made open, darkness has been turned into light, the knot has been split, the arguments of opponents have been shattered, and the eye of the Conqueror’s sons has been restored.”
"It was produced by her; the sectarian teachers were rendered speechless. You have addressed the most excellent among the leaders of the assemblies.
Thus ends the third question, the illustration of the private parts.
